sentences.text: Quillstack is the internal platform that our teams use to publish reports, share datasets and schedule recurring jobs.
This guide explains how to prepare your laptop, connect to the staging environment and run your first job in less than 15 minutes.
You need an active company account and access to the engineering VPN.
If you joined the company in the last 30 days, ask your manager to confirm that your account belongs to the data readers group.
The setup steps below were tested on laptops with at least 16 GB of memory.
Read the security guidelines before you connect any personal device.
They describe which data may leave the office network and which data must stay inside it.
Run the following commands in a terminal.
The installer places a single program in your home directory and does not change any system settings.
When the last command prints a version number, the client is ready.
If it prints an error, open a ticket in Mossgate and attach the full output.
The staging environment mirrors production but only contains synthetic data, so you can experiment freely.
Create a configuration file with the following content:
Then check the connection from the same terminal:
A healthy connection answers in less than 2 seconds.
Slower answers usually mean that the VPN is not active on your laptop.
Choose one of the sample datasets in the catalogue.
Copy its identifier from the details page.
Start the job and wait for the confirmation message.
Every job keeps its logs for 90 days.
You can read them at any time in the Quillstack web console or from the terminal.
Welcome to the Lisbon office.
This handbook collects the practical rules that help a team of 12 people work smoothly across 3 time zones.
It complements the general company policies, which you can find on the policies page.
Most of the team starts work between 8 and 10 in the morning.
We hold a short meeting at 11 every day, and it never lasts longer than 15 minutes.
If you cannot attend, post a written update in the team channel before the meeting starts.
The office has 4 shared laptops for visitors and new colleagues.
Please follow these points every time you use one:
Save the file in your project folder before you continue.
If the screen stays black, restart the application.
Every user gets a personal access code from the IT team.
You can also approve requests from your mobile phone.
Remember to download the latest installer every month.
Shared laptops are wiped every Friday evening, so never keep important work on them.
To request a new monitor, keyboard or headset, follow these steps:
Open the equipment form in Mossgate.
Describe what you need and explain why you need it.
Wait for approval from your team lead, which normally takes 2 working days.
The following example shows the request that the form sends to the internal service.
Do not edit it by hand unless the IT team asks you to do so.
Business travel must be approved at least 14 days in advance.
Keep every receipt and upload it within 30 days of your return.
The complete rules are described in the travel policy, and your team lead can answer most questions about them.
Tarnwave is the gateway that sits in front of every internal service.
It checks access tokens, limits the number of requests per client and records metrics for the operations team.
This page explains how to register a new service and how to test it before you announce it to other teams.
Each service needs a short description file in its repository.
The gateway reads this file during every deployment, so keep it next to your source code.
The name must be unique and may only contain lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
Requests that exceed the limit receive the status code 429 and should be retried after a short pause.
After the deployment, send a test request from your laptop.
Replace the token with one that you generate in the developer portal, and never paste real tokens into chat messages or tickets.
A response with the status code 200 means that the route works.
If you receive the status code 404, the gateway has not loaded your description file yet, so wait 5 minutes and try again.
Tarnwave sends request counts and response times to the metrics dashboard every 60 seconds.
You can find the dashboard for your service at .
An alert is sent to the owning team when more than 5 percent of the requests fail during a period of 10 minutes.
When a service is no longer needed, remove its description file and announce the change at least 7 days before the removal.
Clients that still call the old route will receive the status code 410.
The retirement checklist lists every step, including how to archive the logs.
For questions about the gateway, write to the platform team or check the status page at before you open a ticket.
